title: Spotify billionaire's body scan startup has come to America
key_facts: Neko Health, a Swedish body-scan company co-founded by Spotify's Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne, has opened in New York, TechCrunch reports.
The company has raised nearly $1 billion in total and says its global waitlist tops 300,000 people.
The one-hour scan costs $500, is not covered by insurance, and should qualify for Health Savings Account spending, according to the article.
The scan screens blood, skin and metabolism and uses computer vision; investor Farooq Abbasi says the blood panel grew from 15 biomarkers at his first scan to 55 now.
Neko is eyeing a wider US expansion; TechCrunch notes it still faces scaling and regulatory approval hurdles in the US.
The article is built on an interview with investor Farooq Abbasi of Preface Ventures, who has been scanned twice.
quote_evidence: The company was founded in Sweden, has raised nearly $1 billion total, and just landed in New York.
Currently, Neko health charges $500 for its one-hour scan, which is not covered by insurance
Neko still has a long way to go in the U.S., especially on scaling and regulatory approval.
why_it_matters_hint: A well-funded preventive-scan business is testing whether Americans will pay out of pocket for AI-assisted check-ups the insurance system does not cover.
event_date: Not stated; the New York opening is described as recent in an article dated 3 Oct 2026
notes: Article names the co-founder as 'David Ek'; Spotify's co-founder is Daniel Ek, an apparent slip in the source. Mostly an investor interview; the opening date is not given.
